strategies.name: vwap_trend_continuation_retest
strategies.entry_summary: In a directional session where you already have a long or short bias, wait for price to extend away from VWAP toward the first or second standard-deviation band, then enter in the trend direction after price breaks back and retests the band/VWAP area as support or resistance.
strategies.exit_summary: Use the outer standard-deviation bands as profit targets, specifically the second and third standard deviations. The setup is managed as a continuation trade after the retest in the direction of the session idea.

variants.variant_label: Long continuation after reclaim/retest from discount back toward premium bands
variants.timeframe_note: session-based intraday use, especially around New York open
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to move to at least the first, preferably second, standard deviation, then after it is broken and tested,
variants.target_note: use second and third standard deviations as targets
variants.transcript_quote: you might have a long idea for your session ... after we broke it and tested it we can try our long trade this can be one of the ways to use it andyou

strategies.name: vwap_mean_reversion_from_outer_bands
strategies.entry_summary: When price reaches the outer VWAP standard-deviation bands in an overbought or oversold condition, enter a reversal/mean-reversion trade from those extreme bands expecting price to rebalance back toward fair value.
strategies.exit_summary: Target the central VWAP as the rebalancing objective. The trade idea is specifically to fade the extreme premium/discount move back to session fair value.

variants.variant_label: Fade premium or discount extremes back to VWAP
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: use first/second/outer standard-deviation bands as overbought or oversold institutional reference levels
variants.target_note: central VWAP as target for price rebalancing
variants.transcript_quote: if you're using reversal strategies you might want to use these as some sort of overbought or oversold levels ... and use the central vwap as a target

result.enumeration_note: Two distinct runnable skeletons are taught: a trend-continuation retest setup and an opposite mean-reversion fade; general remarks about VWAP acting as support/resistance are not promoted separately because they lack a standalone runnable exit rule.
